newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler seen posting 10 percent drop in June sales.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler seen posting 10 percent drop in June sales.

text.p: Chrysler Corp. is expected to report a 10 percent drop in June light vehicle sales Tuesday, finishing off a bruising second quarter for the Big Three automakers.

Analysts said Monday that passenger car sales at the No. 3 automaker continued to be soft in June -- possibly falling as much as 20 percent -- as it battles against less-expensive and newer competitive products.
Light truck sales, the category that includes pickup trucks, minivans and sport-utility vehicles, will be down 4 percent to 5 percent at Chrysler, they said.
Despite the declines, Credit Suisse First Boston analyst Nicholas Colas said the numbers indicate an improvement from the nearly 17 percent plunge Chrysler sales took in May.
General Motors Corp. is scheduled to release its June sales on Wednesday, and Ford Motor Co. will report July 3.

Overall, analysts expect June light vehicle sales to fall between 4 percent and 8 percent from a year ago. The seasonally adjusted annual sales rate is forecast to be in the low- to mid-14 million unit range. The rate for both May of 1997 and June 1996 was 14.8 million units.

"Weak used car prices and rising consumer debt levels seem to be winning the tug of war against record employment, consumer confidence and incomes in the battle for new vehicle sales," Burnham Securities Inc. analyst David Healy said in a research report.

The seasonally adjusted selling rate for the second quarter is expected to finish at a weaker-than-expected 14.5 million units. The selling rate for the first quarter was 15.5 million, more robust than many analysts had forecast.
Colas predicts Big Three sales fell 9.4 percent in June while Japanese automakers continued to chip away at the domestics' share of the market.
Healy believes imports and transplants increased their market share to 28.1 percent in June, up from 27.6 percent in May and 25.7 percent in June 1996.
Healy predicts GM's market share fell to 29.2 percent in June from 31.2 percent both in May and a year ago.

Analysts were divided on how far GM's June sales will fall on a unit basis for June. Some predicted a decline of 11 percent to 16 percent. But Mike Luckey, president of Luckey Consulting, believes GM will do better because June is typically a big month for fleet sales.
"I have a feeling there are some big fleet deliveries they are going to count today or tomorrow," he said.
Ford will be the only member of the Big Three posting a sales increase for the month, Luckey said. He predicts Ford's sales will rise modestly as light trucks continue to support weak car sales.
